definitions.gloss: many; a large number of; a lot of (attributive modifier)
definitions.explanation: An attributive phrase formed from the noun {多|おお}く (a great many, a lot) plus the particle の. Used before a noun to mean "many of X" or "a large number of X." More written and formal than たくさんの; a standard choice in news, essays, and academic writing.

examples.japanese: {多|おお}くの⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まった→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
{多|おお}くの⟦{場合|ばあい}→場合：01704_baai⟧、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{方法|ほうほう}→方法：03621_houhou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{有効|ゆうこう}→有効：03645_yuukou⟧だ。
examples.english: In many cases, this method is effective.

examples.japanese: {多|おお}くの⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{卒業|そつぎょう}→卒業：01643_sotsugyou⟧⟦{後|ご}→後：30157_go⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{恩師|おんし}→恩師：12598_onshi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{連絡|れんらく}→連絡：01524_renraku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}り→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Many students continue to stay in touch with their former teachers even after graduation.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{医療|いりょう}→医療：01836_iryou⟧⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧⟦における→〜における：21802_niokeru⟧{多|おお}くの⟦{課題|かだい}→課題：00132_kadai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{解決|かいけつ}する→解決する：17191_kaiketsusuru⟧{手|て}がかり⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{与|あた}えて→与える：01821_ataeru⟧⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: This research provided clues for solving many of the issues facing the medical field.

notes:
Built from the noun {多|おお}く ("many; a lot" — the nominal form of the i-adjective ⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧) + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧. The resulting phrase functions as an attributive modifier, always placed before a noun.

CORE PATTERN:
  {多|おお}くの + noun = "many [noun]" / "a lot of [noun]"

KEY GRAMMATICAL CONTRAST (important!):
⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧ and {多|おお}くの behave differently:
- ⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧ is an i-adjective, but it is NOT used attributively before a noun in modern Japanese: *⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ is unnatural.
- Instead, use {多|おお}くの⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ to mean "many people."
- Or use ⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧ as a predicate: ⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧ ("the people are many / there are many people").

So the choice between {多|おお}くの and ⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧ depends on the position:
- Attributive (before noun): {多|おお}くの + noun
- Predicate (after noun): noun + が/⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ + ⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多|おお}くの⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: many people
- {多|おお}くの⟦{場合|ばあい}→場合：01704_baai⟧: in many cases
- {多|おお}くの⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧: a lot of time
- {多|おお}くの⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧: many problems
- {多|おお}くの⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧: many countries
- {多|おお}くの⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧: many students
- {多|おお}くの⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧: many companies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: many, lots of — conversational; used with both countable and uncountable nouns. More frequent in speech.
- ⟦{大勢|おおぜい}→大勢：02850_oozei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: many (only for people; crowds of people)
- {数|かず}{多|おお}くの: numerous (even more emphatic than {多|おお}くの; written)
- ⟦{数多|あまた}→数多：15498_amata⟧: many (literary; somewhat archaic)
- いろんな / ⟦{様々|さまざま}→様々：01559_samazama⟧な: various (emphasizes variety rather than raw count)

REGISTER:
{多|おお}くの is the standard written and semi-formal choice. It appears in newspapers, essays, textbooks, speeches, and business writing. In everyday conversation, ⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ or simply ⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧ is more natural.

WATCH OUT:
Learners who start from the adjective ⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧ often try *⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ or *⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧. These are ungrammatical in modern Japanese. Whenever you need to say "many X" as a modifier before a noun, use {多|おお}くの + noun.
